newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel leader rejects French troops in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader rejects French troops in east Zaire.

text.p: A rebel leader rejected French troops in eastern Zaire on Friday but said he wanted 500 foreign soldiers to secure a buffer zone between rebels and opponents west of the city of Goma.

"We are asking for soldiers from impartial countries, preferably African. We will not accept the French because they are not impartial. It is clear they have always worked to support the Mobutu regime," Laurent Kabila, head of the Alliance for Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told reporters in the eastern city of Bukavu.
He proposed rebel forces and "the enemy" pull back their forces half a kilometre (550 yards) each from a frontline near Mugunga camp.
"We will withdraw our troops half a kilometre we are asking that the enemy withdraw their troops half a kilometre the other way to create a security zone," said Kabila.
He said the rebels wanted 500 foreign soldiers to secure the proposed buffer zone.
Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has backed a multinational force suggested by France to intervene in eastern Zaire.
Kabila said the rebels managed to push the enemy back near Mugunga on Friday and accused former Hutu Rwandan troops and Interahamwe Hutu extremist militiamen of using refugees as human shields.
He also said the rebels did not want the U.N. refugee agency to take part in operations to help the refugees and accused it of knowing about the rearming of Rwandan refugees in their camps.
